rationale: The 'toml' package is stale (STALE_UPSTREAM, no release in 5 years). Python 3.11+ provides 'tomllib' in the standard library for parsing TOML files, which is the preferred replacement. Since the target Python version is 3.12.14, we can use 'tomllib' and bump the minimum supported Python version to 3.11.
migration_steps: Update the minimum supported Python version to 3.11 in pyproject.toml to enable the use of tomllib.
Replace the 'toml' import with 'tomllib' in linkwatch/config.py.
Update the call to toml.load(path) to use tomllib.load(), which requires opening the file in binary mode.
Remove the 'toml' dependency from pyproject.toml and requirements.txt.

code_edits.why: Replace stale toml package with standard library tomllib.

suggested_tests.name: test_load_settings_migration
suggested_tests.purpose: Verify that load_settings correctly parses a TOML file using tomllib.
suggested_tests.code:
import os
import tempfile
from linkwatch.config import load_settings

def test_load_settings_migration():
    # Create a temporary TOML file
    toml_content = 'title = "test-title"\noutput = "test.html"\n[[sites]]\nname = "test-site"\nurl = "https://test.com"'
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", suffix=".toml", delete=False) as f:
        f.write(toml_content)
        temp_path = f.name
    
    try:
        settings = load_settings(temp_path)
        assert settings.title == "test-title"
        assert settings.output == "test.html"
        assert len(settings.sites) == 1
        assert settings.sites[0].name == "test-site"
        assert settings.sites[0].url == "https://test.com"
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(temp_path):
            os.remove(temp_path)

compatibility_notes: The minimum supported Python version is increased from 3.10 to 3.11.
risks: If the project ever needs to write TOML files (which is not currently observed in the AST scan), tomllib will not be sufficient as it is read-only.
